text: ya its not always upside down so it must be the face itself, idk.
resolution: Diagnosed the 'texture sometimes upside-down on a face' report: confirmed the user's intuition that it's per-face, not a global flip. Each face's default UVs come from faceSquareUV (editMesh.ts) which projects the face loop onto its dominant axis and normalizes to [0,1]² — the resulting U/V orientation falls out of the loop winding + normal sign, which differs across a box's six faces, so the same image lands upright on some faces and rotated/flipped on others. No 'up' convention is applied anywhere. User's workaround (rotate the image in the Studio) is therefore legitimate, not a hack. Offered an optional quality-of-life fix: make box/side faces get a consistent upright default (world-up→V top, world-right→U) in faceSquareUV so posters/signs/frame-backs land upright by default, with top/bottom faces pinned to a fixed orientation. No code changed yet — awaiting the user's call on whether to implement (applies to newly-cooked models) or leave as rotate-when-needed.
